**COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2)**

COVID-19 is a medical condition caused by a virus, specifically a novel coronavirus known as SARS-CoV-2. SARS-CoV-2 has been identified as the causative agent of COVID-19 in individuals, and it is responsible for triggering the characteristic symptoms and severity of the disease. In all cases, SARS-CoV-2 is the direct cause of COVID-19.

The pediatric population, including individuals with persistent hypogammaglobulinemia, are also susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 infection, which can lead to COVID-19. Furthermore, SARS-CoV-2 has been reported to be the causative agent of COVID-19 in pediatric recipients with persistent hypogammaglobulinemia.

It is essential to note that SARS-CoV-2 is the cause of COVID-19, and COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, as they are directly related through a specific pathogenic relationship. The virus is considered the primary agent of disease responsible for COVID-19 outbreaks and cases worldwide.

In summary, COVID-19 is a viral infection caused by SARS-CoV-2, and the two terms are synonymous, with SARS-CoV-2 being the virus responsible for the development of COVID-19 symptoms and severity.
